_comment: Which object in props.glb becomes which prop in the game.
The key is the OBJECT NAME in Blender. Name an object after a prop type -- pine, fir, birch,
rock, boulder, rail, hut, lamp, sign, snowman, fence -- and it is picked up with no entry here
at all. Several objects mapped to the same type are VARIANTS, spread across the map.
SIZE: give ONE of `height`, `length` or `width`, in metres. The scale stays UNIFORM whichever
you pick, so how big you modelled it does not matter, only its proportions do. The rails are
sized by WIDTH here on purpose: they share one cross-section and differ only in length, which
is what small/medium/large should mean, and sizing them by length instead would make the long
one narrower than the board that has to balance on it.
`lod: "far"` marks a low-poly stand-in used past the full-detail radius instead of the real
mesh. Without one, a modelled prop simply stops being drawn out there.
`skip` leaves an object out entirely. Run: node tools/asset-check.mjs
